land.text: Kish and northern Babylonia, taken by Lugal-zage-si who 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa'

successors.note: Sargon, Ur-Zababa's cup-bearer, founded Akkad on this ground c. 2334 (akkadian-empire). The collective dossier sumerian-city-states already draws Sumer and Akkad; this city dossier overlaps it (see notes).

capitals.name: Kish (Tell al-Uhaymir)
capitals.note: '80 km (50 mi) south of Baghdad and 12 km (7.5 mi) east of the ancient city of Babylon'.

correction.text: the city of Kish under its First Dynasty ('c. 2900 – c. 2650 BC'): 'After the flood had swept over, and the kingship had descended from heaven, the kingship was in Kish'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Kish polity. Etana 'reigned c. 2800 BC'; the early names' 'historicity is uncertain'.

correction.text: northern Babylonia around Kish: 'In the north, Semitic populations seem to have been dominant, and Kish may have led a large territorial state' (Early Dynastic page); Enmebaragesi (r. c. 2750), 'the first name confirmed by archaeological finds', 'defeated Elam' (History of Sumer page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, bridged: the pages give a hegemony and a 'large territorial state', not a border; the gazetteer's 'Akkad' (Upper Babylonia) stands for it. The occupations by Lagash (2450–2400) and Uruk (2350–2340) are hatched in the ledger.

ledger.note: 2900 BCE: the First Dynasty of Kish. Dated 'c. 2900 – c. 2650 BC' in the page's list; the Sumerian King List: 'After the flood had swept over, and the kingship had descended from heaven, the kingship was in Kish'.

region.text: northern Babylonia; the Early Dynastic page: 'Kish was possibly the center of a large territorial state'

ledger.note: 2750 BCE: Enmebaragesi's Kish. 'Enmebaragesi: r. c. 2750 BC', 'the first name confirmed by archaeological finds from his reign'; he 'defeated Elam' and built Enlil's temple at Nippur (History of Sumer page); Aga (r. c. 2700) fought Gilgamesh, and 'Then Kish was defeated and the kingship was taken to Eanna (Uruk)'. The territory is bridged.

2450 BCE: Eannatum of Lagash takes Kish. 'He defeated Kish, Akshak, and Mari from the Antasurra of Ningirsu' and 'claimed the title of King of Kish'; Zuzu of Akshak 'r. c. 2470 BC', 'temp. of Eannatum' (Kish page). Mesilim (r. c. 2550) had earlier arbitrated between Lagash and Umma.

2400 BCE: Kug-Bau's Kish is independent again. She 'is said to have gained independence from En-anna-tum I of Lagash and En-shag-kush-ana of Uruk' (c. 2400 BC); the Eannatum page: Kish 'regained its independence after his death'. Kish III c. 2430–2360.

2350 BCE: Enshakushanna of Uruk seizes Kish. He 'seized Kish and imprisoned its king Embi-Ishtar around 2350 B.C.'; the Uruk page: Enshakushanna (c. 2350) 'lord of Sumer and king of all the land'. Uruk's hegemony is the collective dossier's.
2340 BCE: the occupation ends in annexation (next event). Puzur-Suen (r. c. 2360) and Ur-Zababa (r. c. 2340) of Kish IV ruled between.

2340 BCE: Lugal-zage-si overthrows Ur-Zababa. He 'invaded Kish, where he overthrew Ur-Zababa'; 'Ur-Zababa: r. c. 2340 BC (6 years)', 'Sargon of Akkad was his cup-bearer' (Kish page). Kish IV 'c. 2360 – c. 1897 BC' continues as a city under Akkad (Manishtushu 'Lugal Kish'; Iphur-Kish led the Great Revolt c. 2254), Ur III ('governed by an ensi appointed by the kings of Ur'), as 'a buffer state' c. 2020–1900 and under Babylon from Sumu-abum (c. 1897–1883) to Sin-muballit.

wars.name: Eannatum's campaigns
wars.outcome: Kish defeated and held by Lagash; Eannatum 'claimed the title of King of Kish'; Kish 'regained its independence after his death'.

wars.name: Enshakushanna's seizure of Kish
wars.outcome: Enshakushanna of Uruk 'seized Kish and imprisoned its king Embi-Ishtar around 2350 B.C.'.

wars.name: Lugal-zage-si's conquest of Kish
wars.outcome: Ur-Zababa overthrown; Kish absorbed into Lugal-zage-si's kingdom, then Sargon's Akkad.

certainty.note: A city and a hegemony ('King of Kish'); no page draws a border.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: Kish from its First Dynasty (c. 2900) to Ur-Zababa's overthrow by Lugal-zage-si (c. 2340). The territory is bridged throughout (confidence 1): the pages give the Sumerian King List's hegemony, Enmebaragesi's Elamite war and 'a large territorial state' in the north, never a border; the gazetteer's 'Akkad' region stands for northern Babylonia. The Kish page dates Mesilim c. 2550 and Enmebaragesi c. 2750 where other pages give c. 2500 and c. 2600. Overlaps the collective dossier sumerian-city-states (see the batch report). Kish IV's later city life under Akkad, Ur III, Isin-Larsa and Babylon is not a state.
